question: In which state is the Chithirai festival celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chithirai Festival (Chithirai Thiruvizha) is celebrated at the Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. (चिथिरई उत्सव — तमिलनाडु)

 

• It is held in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April–May) and commemorates the celestial marriage (Thirukalyanam) of the goddess Meenakshi to Lord Sundareswarar (Shiva).

 

• The festival also incorporates the legend of Lord Alagar (Vishnu) crossing the Vaigai river to attend his sister Meenakshi's wedding, symbolising the meeting of Shaivite and Vaishnavite traditions.

 

• It is one of the oldest and largest temple festivals of South India, attracting lakhs of pilgrims and tourists each year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Madurai Meenakshi Temple is dedicated to Meenakshi (Parvati) and her consort Sundareswarar; its gopurams are famous examples of Dravidian temple architecture.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for festivals like Baisakhi and Lohri, not Chithirai.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Known for festivals like Teej and Gangaur; Chithirai is not associated with Rajasthan.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 4): Known for festivals like Wangala and Behdeinkhlam; Chithirai is not celebrated there.

question: Kalbelia dance is generally performed in which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalbelia dance is a folk dance performed by the Kalbelia (snake charmer) tribe of Rajasthan. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• It is performed by women in flowing black skirts (adorned with silver thread embroidery) who dance to the accompaniment of instruments like the been (pungi), dholak and khanjari, mimicking the movements of a serpent.

 

• Kalbelia songs and dances of Rajasthan were inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Chari and Terah Taali.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Known for Bharatanatyam and Karagattam, not Kalbelia.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Known for Bhangra and Giddha.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Known for Bihu dance.

question: The rule of the English East India company was ended in British India under the Government of India Act, ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1858.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The rule of the English East India Company in India ended under the Government of India Act, 1858. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858 — ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी शासन की समाप्ति)

 

• The Act was passed by the British Parliament in the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857, transferring the administration of India from the East India Company to the British Crown.

 

• It created the post of Secretary of State for India, assisted by a 15-member Council of India, and the Governor-General of India was additionally given the title of Viceroy; Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The transfer of power was formally announced through Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1 November 1858.

 

NOTE

 

• 1857 (Option 2): The year of the Revolt of 1857 (First War of Independence), not the year of the Act.

 

• 1859 (Option 3): No such Government of India Act was passed in this year.

 

• 1856 (Option 4): Lord Canning became Governor-General in 1856, but the Act ending Company rule came in 1858.

question: Which of the following is a highly electropositive element that readily gives up an electron in order to obtain a stable electronic configuration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Na.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium (Na) is an alkali metal and is highly electropositive, readily losing its single valence electron to attain a stable, noble-gas-like electronic configuration. (सोडियम — विद्युत धनात्मक तत्व)

 

• Electropositivity is the tendency of an atom to lose electrons and form positive ions (cations); it is highest for elements on the extreme left of the periodic table (alkali and alkaline earth metals).

 

• Sodium has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1; by losing the single outer electron it achieves the stable configuration of neon (2, 8), forming the Na⁺ ion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electronegativity (the tendency to gain electrons) is highest for elements on the extreme right of the periodic table (halogens), opposite to electropositivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Cl (Option 1): A halogen; it is electronegative, tending to gain an electron rather than lose one.

 

• O (Option 2): Oxygen is also electronegative, gaining electrons to complete its octet.

 

• N (Option 4): Nitrogen is a non-metal and is electronegative, not electropositive.

question: The famous scientist, Albert Einstein, was inspired by whose idea of non-violence?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The scientist Albert Einstein was deeply inspired and moved by Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and Satyagraha. (महात्मा गांधी — अहिंसा)

 

• Einstein famously remarked about Gandhi: "Generations to come will scarce believe that such a one as this ever in flesh and blood walked upon this earth."

 

• Gandhi's method of non-violent civil disobedience, drawn partly from ideas of Ahimsa in Indian philosophy and thinkers like Leo Tolstoy, went on to influence global leaders such as Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela as well as scientists like Einstein.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi led India's freedom struggle through movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) and Quit India Movement (1942).

 

NOTE

 

• Vardhaman Mahavira (Option 2): The 24th Jain Tirthankara, associated with the doctrine of Ahimsa in Jainism, but he is not the figure Einstein specifically praised.

 

• Gautam Buddha (Option 3): Founder of Buddhism, preached non-violence, but Einstein's remarks on non-violence were specifically about Gandhi.

 

• BR Ambedkar (Option 4): Chief architect of the Indian Constitution; not associated with inspiring Einstein's views on non-violence.

question: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY matched?
option_1: Montane climate - Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand
option_2: Tropical monsoon climate - The Western Ghats, the Malabar Coast and southern Assam
option_3: Tropical semi-arid (steppe) climate - Karnataka, central Maharashtra, some parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
option_4: Hot deserts, arid climate - Rajasthan and some parts of Gujarat
solution_text:
The correct answer is Montane climate - Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This pairing is incorrect. In India, Montane (Mountain) climate is found in the Himalayan region — states like Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and the hilly parts of West Bengal (Darjeeling) and the North-East — not in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand, which lie largely in the plains/plateau region. (पर्वतीय (मोंटेन) जलवायु — हिमालयी क्षेत्र)

 

• Montane climate is characterised by a decrease in temperature with increasing altitude, giving rise to a succession of climatic types from tropical to tundra within a short vertical distance.

 

• The three remaining options correctly describe climate types found in India — the Tropical monsoon climate of the Western Ghats/Malabar Coast/southern Assam, the Tropical semi-arid (steppe) climate of the Deccan interior, and the Hot desert climate of western Rajasthan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's climate is broadly classified into Tropical Rainforest, Tropical Savanna, Tropical Monsoon, Tropical Semi-arid (Steppe), Hot Desert, Humid Sub-tropical and Mountain (Montane) types.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: Correctly matched — the Western Ghats, Malabar Coast and southern Assam experience Tropical monsoon climate with heavy rainfall.

 

• Option 3: Correctly matched — Karnataka, central Maharashtra and parts of Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh (rain-shadow Deccan interior) experience Tropical semi-arid (steppe) climate.

 

• Option 4: Correctly matched — western Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat (Kutch) experience Hot desert, arid climate.

question: Diwan-i-Arz was essentially the department of ________ under Delhi Sultanate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is military services.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diwan-i-Arz was the military department of the Delhi Sultanate, responsible for the recruitment, organisation, and inspection of the army. (दीवान-ए-अर्ज़ — सैन्य विभाग)

 

• It was headed by the Ariz-i-Mumalik, who supervised the maintenance of the royal army, fixed the salaries of soldiers, and inspected troops and horses.

 

• The department was formally organised/strengthened under Sultan Balban and further systematised by Alauddin Khalji, who introduced measures like the branding of horses (dagh) and descriptive rolls (chehra) of soldiers to prevent fraud.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key departments of the Delhi Sultanate include Diwan-i-Wizarat (finance, headed by the Wazir), Diwan-i-Insha (royal correspondence) and Diwan-i-Risalat (religious affairs/appeals).

 

NOTE

 

• financial services (Option 1): This was the function of the Diwan-i-Wizarat, headed by the Wazir.

 

• court ceremonies (Option 2): Court ceremonies and etiquette were generally overseen by officials like the Barbak/Wakil-i-dar, not the Diwan-i-Arz.

 

• royal karkhanas (Option 4): The royal workshops (karkhanas) were supervised separately, not by the Diwan-i-Arz.

question: What is the full form of IADP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intensive Agricultural District Programme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• IADP stands for Intensive Agricultural District Programme, launched in 1960-61 on the recommendation of the Ford Foundation team. (गहन कृषि जिला कार्यक्रम — IADP)

 

• It is also known as the "Package Programme" because it provided a package of improved inputs (better seeds, fertilizers, credit, irrigation and extension services) in selected districts to maximise agricultural production.

 

• The programme was initially launched in seven districts (later extended), including Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu), Raipur (then Madhya Pradesh), Ludhiana (Punjab), Shahabad (Bihar), Aligarh (UP), West Godavari (Andhra Pradesh) and Pali (Rajasthan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• IADP was followed by the Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP) in 1964-65, extending similar inputs to a wider set of areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Agricultural Development Programme (Option 2): Not the correct expansion of IADP; no such official programme name exists.

 

• Integrated Agricultural District Plan (Option 3): Incorrect expansion; the correct term is 'Intensive', not 'Integrated', and 'Programme', not 'Plan'.

 

• Intensive Agricultural Development Project (Option 4): Incorrect; the correct phrase is 'District Programme', not 'Development Project'.

question: Who among the following has been appointed as the new Chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), for a period of four years or until he attains the age of 70 years, whichever is the earliest in November 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Ashok Bhushan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Ashok Bhushan, a former Supreme Court judge, was appointed as the Chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), for a period of four years or until he attains the age of 70, whichever is earlier. (न्यायमूर्ति अशोक भूषण — NCLAT अध्यक्ष)

 

• The NCLAT was constituted under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013 to hear appeals against orders of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and also functions as the appellate authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 and the Competition Act, 2002.

 

• Justice Bhushan retired from the Supreme Court of India in July 2021 before taking up the NCLAT chairpersonship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NCLAT is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Justice Vikram Nath (Option 1): A former Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court, later elevated as a Supreme Court judge; not the NCLAT Chairperson appointed in 2021.

 

• Justice BV Nagarathna (Option 2): A Supreme Court judge, in line to become India's first woman Chief Justice of India in 2027; not associated with the NCLAT chairpersonship.

 

• Justice Abhay Oka (Option 4): A Supreme Court judge (formerly Chief Justice of Karnataka High Court); not the NCLAT Chairperson.

question: Under which policy has the Union Ministry of Power launched a scheme for procurement of aggregate power of 4500 MW for five years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shakti Policy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Union Ministry of Power launched a scheme for the procurement of aggregate power of 4,500 MW for five years under clause B(v) of the SHAKTI Policy. (शक्ति नीति — विद्युत मंत्रालय)

 

• SHAKTI stands for Scheme for Harnessing and Allocating Koyla (Coal) Transparently in India, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2017 to streamline and bring transparency to coal allocation for the power sector.

 

• This particular scheme was aimed at helping power-generating companies that did not have Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) or fuel supply agreements, by providing coal linkages against long-term/medium-term power procurement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SHAKTI Policy replaced the earlier practice of allocating captive coal blocks and linkages in an ad hoc manner.

 

NOTE

 

• Urja Sanchay Policy (Option 1): Not a real scheme related to this power procurement; a distractor option.

 

• Nai Urja Policy (Option 3): Not a real, officially notified scheme of the Ministry of Power for this purpose.

 

• Gatishakti Policy (Option 4): PM GatiShakti is a National Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity/infrastructure, launched in 2021 — unrelated to coal-linked power procurement.

question: Which element was arbitrarily assigned a value of 4.0 in the 'Halogens' section in 1922 by Linus Pauling, an American scientist?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fluorine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Linus Pauling, an American scientist, developed the Pauling electronegativity scale, in which Fluorine was arbitrarily assigned the highest value of 4.0. (फ्लोरीन — पॉलिंग विद्युत ऋणात्मकता पैमाना)

 

• Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table, being small in size with a strong tendency to attract shared electrons.

 

• All other elements' electronegativity values on the Pauling scale are calibrated relative to fluorine's benchmark value of 4.0.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electronegativity generally increases across a period (left to right) and decreases down a group in the periodic table.

 

NOTE

 

• Iodine (Option 2): A halogen but has a much lower electronegativity (~2.66) than fluorine due to its larger atomic size.

 

• Astatine (Option 3): The heaviest, rarest halogen, with very low electronegativity among halogens.

 

• Bromine (Option 4): A halogen with electronegativity (~2.96), lower than fluorine's benchmark 4.0 value.

question: The MITRA scheme was first announced in the Union Budget for 2021-22 to set up world-class infrastructure in which sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Textile industry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The MITRA (Mega Investment Textiles Parks) scheme was first announced in the Union Budget 2021-22 to set up 7 world-class Mega Investment Textile Parks across India over three years. (मित्र योजना — वस्त्र उद्योग)

 

• MITRA stands for Mega Investment Textiles Parks, aimed at creating world-class infrastructure with plug-and-play facilities to enable global textile manufacturing champions and boost exports and employment.

 

• The scheme complements the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for textiles, together aimed at making India's textile sector globally competitive.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some of the states where PM MITRA parks have been approved include Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Automobiles (Option 1): Supported instead by schemes like the PLI scheme for Automobile and Auto Components, not MITRA.

 

• Defence manufacturing (Option 3): Supported through initiatives like Defence Industrial Corridors, not the MITRA scheme.

 

• Pharmaceuticals (Option 4): Supported through the PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals and Bulk Drug Parks, not MITRA.

question: Where in India are the Sundari trees that provide durable and hard timber found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mangrove Forests.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes), which provides durable and hard timber, is found in the Mangrove (Tidal) Forests of the Sundarbans delta in West Bengal. (सुंदरी वृक्ष — सुंदरबन डेल्टा, मैंग्रोव वन)

 

• The Sundarbans, formed at the delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna river system, derives its name from the abundant Sundari trees found there and is the largest mangrove forest in the world.

 

• Sundari wood is valued for boat-building, house construction and furniture due to its hardness and durability, and is resistant to decay in the waterlogged, saline mangrove environment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

 

NOTE

 

• Tropical Deciduous Forests (Option 1): Dominated by trees like Teak and Sal, found in regions with moderate rainfall — not where Sundari trees grow.

 

• Montane Forests (Option 3): Found in the Himalayan highland regions with coniferous/temperate species, unrelated to Sundari trees.

 

• Tropical Evergreen Forests (Option 4): Found in high-rainfall regions like the Western Ghats and North-East India, characterised by species like rosewood and ebony, not Sundari.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in domestic income?
option_1: Income earned by the residents of the country
option_2: Income earned by the non-residents outside the country
option_3: Income earned by all the employees of the country
option_4: Profit of all the industries of the country
solution_text:
The correct answer is Income earned by the non-residents outside the country.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Domestic income (Net/Gross Domestic Product) refers to the sum of factor incomes (rent, wages, interest, profit) generated within the domestic territory of a country, irrespective of whether they are earned by residents or non-residents. (घरेलू आय — घरेलू क्षेत्र)

 

• Since income earned by non-residents outside the country is generated outside the domestic territory, it can never form a part of that country's domestic income — it is, by definition, excluded.

 

• In contrast, income earned by residents within the country, income earned by all employees working within the domestic territory, and profits of industries located within the country are all part of domestic income, since they are generated inside the domestic territory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Income = Domestic Income + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA), where NFIA accounts for income earned by residents from abroad minus income earned by non-residents within the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Income earned by the residents of the country (Option 1): This is a part of domestic income, as it is generated within the domestic territory.

 

• Income earned by all the employees of the country (Option 3): This is included in domestic income as a component of factor income (compensation of employees) generated domestically.

 

• Profit of all the industries of the country (Option 4): Profit generated by industries located within the domestic territory is a component of domestic income.

question: As per National Family Health Survey (NFHS 5) 2019-21, what percentage of women have a bank or savings account that they themselves use?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 78.6%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 2019-21, 78.6% of women (age 15-49) in India have a bank or savings account that they themselves use. (राष्ट्रीय परिवार स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण-5 — 78.6% महिलाएं)

 

• This marks a significant rise from 53% in NFHS-4 (2015-16), reflecting the impact of financial inclusion drives such as the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY).

 

• The increase was particularly sharp in rural areas, where the figure rose from about 48.5% (NFHS-4) to around 77% (NFHS-5), narrowing the rural-urban gap in women's financial inclusion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NFHS-5 (2019-21) was conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, covering all States/UTs of India, and also collects data on health, nutrition and other demographic indicators.

 

NOTE

 

• 68.3% (Option 1), 87.7% (Option 3) and 58.5% (Option 4): These figures do not match the NFHS-5 (2019-21) reported value of 78.6% for women having and using a bank/savings account.

question: Tansen, who was included in the Navaratnas of Akbar, was an expert in playing which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tansen (Miyan Tansen), one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) of Emperor Akbar's court, was an accomplished vocalist and was particularly noted as an expert player of the Rabab (rebab), a plucked string instrument. (तानसेन — रबाब वादक)

 

• Tansen is regarded as one of the greatest musicians in Indian history, credited with composing several ragas (such as Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar and Darbari Kanada) that are still performed today.

 

• He belonged to the Dhrupad tradition of Hindustani classical music and served in the courts of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa before joining Akbar's court around 1562.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other Navaratnas of Akbar's court included Abul Fazl, Faizi, Raja Birbal, Raja Todar Mal, Raja Man Singh, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, Fakir Aziao-Din and Mullah Do Piaza.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagada (Option 1): A large kettledrum, a percussion instrument — not the instrument Tansen was renowned for.

 

• Veena (Option 2): A plucked string instrument, but Tansen's fame as an instrumentalist is particularly tied to the rabab, not the veena.

 

• Sarangi (Option 3): A bowed string instrument, not the instrument associated with Tansen's expertise.

question:
Match the following countries with respect to their ranking on the Global Hunger Index 2022 out of 121 countries.

Country          Rank

1. India          a. 99

2. Pakistan       b. 107

3. Nepal          c. 81
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-b, 2-a, 3-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2022 (out of 121 countries), India ranked 107th (b), Pakistan ranked 99th (a), and Nepal ranked 81st (c). (वैश्विक भूख सूचकांक 2022 — भारत 107वें स्थान पर)

 

• India's rank fell sharply from 101st in 2021 to 107th in 2022, placing it behind neighbours such as Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, though ahead of war-torn Afghanistan.

 

• The Global Hunger Index is published jointly every year by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany), and is calculated using four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, and child mortality.

 

Therefore, the correct matching is 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, i.e., the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India contested the GHI 2022 methodology, particularly its reliance on an opinion-poll-based estimate of undernourishment.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (1-c, 2-a, 3-b): Incorrect — wrongly assigns rank 81 to India and rank 107 to Nepal.

 

• Option 2 (1-b, 2-c, 3-a): Incorrect — wrongly assigns rank 81 to Pakistan and rank 99 to Nepal.

 

• Option 3 (1-a, 2-b, 3-c): Incorrect — wrongly assigns rank 99 to India and rank 107 to Pakistan (the two are swapped).

question: Mitochondria is NOT found in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bacteria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitochondria are membrane-bound cell organelles found in eukaryotic cells; they are absent in bacteria, which are prokaryotes. (माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया — जीवाणु में अनुपस्थित)

 

• Bacteria lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, chloroplasts, and the endoplasmic reticulum; instead, respiration occurs across the cell membrane (mesosomes).

 

• Yeast, algae and fungi are all eukaryotic organisms and therefore possess mitochondria, which perform aerobic respiration and are known as the "powerhouse of the cell".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mitochondria have their own circular DNA and ribosomes and are believed to have originated from free-living bacteria via endosymbiosis.

 

NOTE

 

• yeast (Option 1): A unicellular eukaryotic fungus; it contains mitochondria.

 

• algae (Option 3): Eukaryotic organisms; they possess mitochondria (and chloroplasts).

 

• fungi (Option 4): Eukaryotic organisms; fungal cells contain mitochondria.

question:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding the terminology used in the Parliament?

A.Appropriation Bill — A Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India

B.Demand for Grants — Earmarking of budgetary allocation for meeting only planned expenditure of a Ministry/Department

C.Short Duration Discussion — For raising a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for which a notice has to be given by a Member and supported by 50 Members
solution_text:
The correct answer is A only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: An Appropriation Bill is a Money Bill passed by Parliament to provide for the withdrawal/appropriation of money from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India, to meet the expenditure voted through the Demands for Grants and the charged expenditure. (विनियोग विधेयक — भारत की संचित निधि)

 

• Statement B is incorrect: A Demand for Grant is the request for funds, presented ministry/department-wise in the Union Budget, for meeting the entire voted expenditure (both revenue and capital) of that ministry/department — it is not limited to "only planned expenditure".

 

• Statement C is incorrect: A Short Duration Discussion (Rule 193, Lok Sabha) allows a member to raise discussion on a matter of urgent public importance through a notice that must be supported by at least two other members, not fifty members.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike Short Duration Discussions, a motion such as a No-Confidence Motion requires the support of at least 50 members to be admitted for discussion in the Lok Sabha.

 

NOTE

 

• A, B and C (Option 1): Incorrect, as it wrongly includes B and C, both of which have factual errors.

 

• B and C only (Option 2): Incorrect, as neither B nor C is correctly stated.

 

• A and C only (Option 4): Incorrect, as it wrongly includes C, which misstates the member-support requirement for a Short Duration Discussion.

question: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2020 was awarded to Meenakshi Chitharanjan for her contribution to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meenakshi Chitharanjan was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2020 for her contribution to Bharatanatyam. (मीनाक्षी चित्हरंजन — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She is a noted exponent of the Pandanallur style/bani (gharana) of Bharatanatyam, a classical dance tradition associated with the temple town of Pandanallur in Tamil Nadu.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, confers this award annually to recognise excellence in the performing arts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu, traditionally performed as a temple art.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 2): A classical dance of Odisha; not the field for which Meenakshi Chitharanjan was honoured.

 

• Manipuri (Option 3): A classical dance of Manipur; unrelated to her area of expertise.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 4): A classical dance of Andhra Pradesh; not the dance form associated with her.

question: Select the INCORRECT statement about Phylum Arthropoda.
option_1: Class Insecta is the largest class of Phylum Arthropoda.
option_2: Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.
option_3: Over 85% of all the known animal species are arthropods.
option_4: Phylum Arthropoda comprises a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is incorrect — the main component of the exoskeleton of arthropods is chitin (a nitrogenous polysaccharide), not lignin. Lignin is a complex organic polymer found in the cell walls of plants (especially wood), not in animal exoskeletons. (काइटिन — संधिपाद बहिःकंकाल)

 

• Phylum Arthropoda is characterised by a hard, chitinous exoskeleton and jointed (articulated) appendages, which is where the phylum's name derives from (Greek: arthron = joint, podos = foot).

 

• Class Insecta is indeed the largest class of Phylum Arthropoda (and the largest class in the animal kingdom), and arthropods make up over 85% of all known animal species, making the other three statements correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other phyla-defining features of Arthropoda include a segmented body, an open circulatory system, and bilateral symmetry; examples include insects, crustaceans, arachnids and myriapods.

 

NOTE

 

• Class Insecta is the largest class of Phylum Arthropoda (Option 1): This statement is correct — Insecta contains the most species of any class in the animal kingdom.

 

• Over 85% of all the known animal species are arthropods (Option 3): This statement is correct — arthropods are the most species-rich phylum on Earth.

 

• Phylum Arthropoda comprises a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages (Option 4): This statement is correct — it describes the defining characteristics of the phylum.

question: ________ countries participated in the Tokyo Paralympic 2020.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 162.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A total of 162 delegations/National Paralympic Committees (NPCs) participated in the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic), surpassing the 159 delegations that competed at Rio 2016. (टोक्यो पैरालंपिक 2020 — 162 देश)

 

• The Games were held in Tokyo, Japan, from 24 August to 5 September 2021, and included the debut of Refugee Paralympic Team athletes.

 

• India sent its largest-ever Paralympic contingent and won a record 19 medals (5 gold, 8 silver, 6 bronze) at the Tokyo Paralympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tokyo Summer Olympics 2020 (also postponed to 2021) preceded the Paralympics and was held from 23 July to 8 August 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• 163 (Option 1), 161 (Option 2) and 164 (Option 3): These figures do not match the officially reported number of 162 participating delegations at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.

question: Who sent the Greek ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seleucus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador and historian, was sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra by the Greek/Hellenistic ruler Seleucus I Nicator. (मेगस्थनीज — सेल्यूकस निकेटर)

 

• This followed the peace treaty between Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus I Nicator (a former general of Alexander the Great) around 303 BCE, under which Seleucus ceded territories in the northwest in exchange for war elephants and a matrimonial alliance.

 

• Megasthenes recorded his observations of Mauryan India in his famous work "Indica", which, though now lost in original form, survives through fragments quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE, with the guidance of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

 

NOTE

 

• Tolmi (Option 2): Not a historical figure associated with this event; a distractor option.

 

• Dionysus (Option 3): A Greek god associated with wine, not a historical ruler who sent Megasthenes.

 

• Sikandar (Option 4): The Persian/Indian name for Alexander the Great, who invaded India in 326 BCE, but it was Seleucus (his successor in the East), not Alexander, who sent Megasthenes.

question: Which of the following amendment acts included Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42nd Amendment Act.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added Part IVA (Article 51A) to the Constitution, incorporating Fundamental Duties of citizens, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. (42वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added; an 11th duty (regarding parents'/guardians' duty to provide education to children aged 6-14) was later added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• The 42nd Amendment is often called the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made, including additions to the Preamble (adding "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity") and changes to Centre-State relations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and, unlike Fundamental Rights, are not legally enforceable in a court of law.

 

NOTE

 

• 40th Amendment Act (Option 1): Related to vesting of rights over resources of the continental shelf/exclusive economic zone in the Union; unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

 

• 41st Amendment Act (Option 3): Raised the retirement age of members of state Public Service Commissions; unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

 

• 39th Amendment Act (Option 4): Placed the election of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial review; unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

question: Which of the following states recognise the Dahi Handi as a sports event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maharashtra officially recognises Dahi Handi as an adventure sport, a status granted by the Maharashtra government in 2017. (दही हांडी — महाराष्ट्र, साहसिक खेल)

 

• Dahi Handi is celebrated as part of the Krishna Janmashtami festivities, where young men (known as "Govindas") form human pyramids to break a pot (handi) of curd/butter suspended at a height, re-enacting the childhood exploits of Lord Krishna.

 

• Recognising it as a sport allowed participants (Govinda pathaks) to be treated as sportspersons, opening avenues for injury compensation, sports quota benefits and government support.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tradition of Dahi Handi is especially prominent in Mumbai, Thane and Pune in Maharashtra, where competing Govinda pathaks vie to break the highest-hung handis with prize money.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Dahi Handi is not a recognised sports event associated with Bihar.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Not the state associated with official recognition of Dahi Handi as a sport.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Krishna Janmashtami is widely celebrated (notably in Mathura/Vrindavan), but Dahi Handi as a state-recognised sport is specific to Maharashtra.
